gaps.sentence: It is one of the most impressive buildings ___ I have ever seen.
gaps.explanation: After superlative expressions, 'that' is the standard relative pronoun in defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: The house at the end of the street, ___ has been empty for years, is for sale.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clauses about things take 'which'; 'who' is for people and 'that' is not allowed here.

gaps.sentence: He is a colleague on ___ you can always depend.
gaps.explanation: After 'on', the formal relative pronoun for a person is 'whom'.

gaps.sentence: July and August are the months ___ most Italians take their holidays.
gaps.explanation: 'When' means 'in which' after time expressions; the clause describes when the action happens.

gaps.sentence: The woman ___ won the prize gave a short speech.
gaps.explanation: The gap is the subject pronoun for a person, so 'who' is needed; 'whose' would show possession.

gaps.sentence: Anyone ___ wants to join the trip should sign up today.
gaps.explanation: 'Anyone who' is the standard pattern; 'who' is the subject pronoun for people.

gaps.sentence: The new bridge, ___ cost two billion euros, opened last month.
gaps.hint: thing + extra information after a comma
gaps.explanation: 'Which' introduces non-defining clauses about things; 'that' is forbidden there.

gaps.sentence: My uncle, ___ lives in Canada, is coming to stay next week.
gaps.hint: non-defining clause after a comma about a person
gaps.explanation: In non-defining clauses (between commas) 'that' is not allowed; 'who' refers to people.
